These are express operative immigration-specific recommendation/monitoring functions, not only findings or the fact DHS is a member. The proposal does not itself order a named person removed, adjudicate unlawful status, redefine sanctuary city, create a new admission/removal ground, directly repeal DC sanctuary legislation or newly grant the Commission the underlying agencies arrest, detention or deportation powers. Its operational-assistance/coordination permission is expressly TO THE EXTENT PERMITTED BY LAW. Commission membership includes nine specified Federal departments/components or U.S. Attorney offices, the DC Executive Office of the Mayor AS DEFINED in 1-315.02(3), and additional Federal entities chosen by the chair. That DC definition covers specified managerial/budget/personnel/secretarial/planning/information/special-support offices and excludes the named Office of Personnel; it is not every DC agency or a requirement for the Mayor personally to serve. Heads designate representatives within 45 days, including 45 days after later chair designations for added Federal entities. The President designates a SENIOR EOP official as chair within 45 days, with meeting scheduling/entity selection and a consultatively developed charter submitted within 7 days of completion. The Commission reports its carried-out functions/authorities and appropriate legislative recommendations to the specified House Oversight and Senate Homeland Security committees, without an invented periodic reporting deadline. Its other tasks concern forensic-lab accreditation, police staffing/capabilities, concealed-carry-license processing, qualified pretrial policies, transit crime and law-enforcement presence; they are whole-package context, not independently attributed Immigration component choices. The exact H.R.1689 EH proposal directs the Secretary of Homeland Security, notwithstanding any other law, to designate Haiti for temporary protected status until the date three months after January 20, 2029—April 20, 2029. It is a mandatory country-specific designation for that stated duration rather than a newly created TPS program or a direction to apply only ordinary discretionary six-to-eighteen-month designation periods. It does not state that Haiti has never before been designated or resolve litigation/agency decisions about earlier designations. The existing 8 USC 1254a framework, read with enacted Public Law 119-21 sections 100001/100003(c)/100006 rather than unqualified 2024 text, distinguishes designation of a country from granting TPS to an individual national (or stateless person last habitually resident there). Individual eligibility requires continuous U.S. physical presence since the effective date of the most recent designation, residence since the designated date, registration, applicable admissibility and absence of statutory bars, with stated brief/casual/innocent absence and emergency-trip qualifications. The bill does not supply individual presence/residence/registration dates or remove these requirements. Existing bars include a U.S.-committed felony or at least two misdemeanors and the incorporated persecution, particularly serious crime, serious nonpolitical foreign crime, security/terrorism and firm-resettlement grounds. Existing admissibility exceptions and individual humanitarian/family-unity/public-interest waivers retain their specified nonwaivable criminal/security boundaries. TPS may be withdrawn for ineligibility, disqualifying absence or registration failure without good cause. The enacted 2025 law raised the authorized TPS registration-fee ceiling from $50 to $500, subject to fiscal 2026-and-later annual CPI adjustments rounded to the next lower $10 multiple, and prohibits waiver/reduction of required TPS fees. This is an adjusted statutory ceiling, not a claimed current agency fee quote. A separate additional fee for an initial TPS employment-authorization application starts in fiscal 2025 at the greater of $550 or an amount DHS establishes by rule, with annual CPI adjustments and no fee waiver/reduction. Each initial employment authorization is valid for one year or the TPS duration, whichever is shorter. The country-designation endpoint does not guarantee one employment document through April 2029; actual charged amounts, renewals or document issuance are not inferred. For a person granted TPS, the existing framework supplies protection from removal during the status period and employment authorization; it does not itself grant permanent residence or citizenship, guarantee all public benefits or authorize a person abroad to enter to apply. Its status-based detention protection, consent-based travel and adjustment-status provisions keep their own limits. This bill imposes the country-duration mandate, not individual awards or actual implementation, removals, benefit outcomes or enactment.

The complete H.R. 6260 EH makes one insertion in 18 USC 1033(f)(1)(A): the writing of insurance would explicitly include the posting of monetary bail, criminal bail bonds and FEDERAL IMMIGRATION BAIL BONDS. It changes the defined business activity used by existing 1033 criminal provisions; it is not merely a criminal defendant being a noncitizen. The explicit immigration-bond posting scope establishes the candidate Immigration connection. Retained 1033(f) defines insurer and business activities, including necessary/incidental acts and specified representatives, and interstate commerce broadly with DC/territory/possession and cross-boundary/other federal-jurisdiction routes. The proposal does not declare every private cash gift, every nonprofit bail fund or every bond provider an insurer regardless of the retained definitions/jurisdiction. Existing 1033(a) requires covered-business interstate-commerce activity and a KNOWING/intent-to-deceive false material financial statement or WILLFUL material overvaluation, with the specified regulatory-report nexus and purpose; its ordinary maximum imprisonment is 10 years, with the separately harm-conditioned insurer-conservation/rehabilitation/liquidation 15 year route. Existing(b) requires covered-person/transaction scope and WILLFUL misappropriation; ordinary 10 year and qualified 15 year routes differ from the not-over$5,000 one-year maximum. Existing(c) requires KNOWING material false-entry conduct with INTENT TO DECEIVE about financial condition/solvency and its covered scope, again with distinct ordinary/qualified imprisonment routes. Existing(d) requires CORRUPT threats/force/communication obstruction or endeavor concerning a pending covered regulatory proceeding;10 year maximum. Existing(e)(1)(A) requires a prior criminal felony involving dishonesty/breach of trust OR a 1033 conviction AND WILLFUL engagement/participation in covered insurance business; it is not every arrest, conviction or felony. Its ordinary maximum is 5 years, and(e)(1)(B) addresses covered-business individuals who WILLFULLY permit that prohibited participation. Existing(e)(2) permits the otherwise described person to participate with WRITTEN CONSENT from an insurance regulatory official authorized to regulate the insurer that specifically refers to(e). All imprisonment clauses retain fine OR imprisonment OR both; none is an automatic mandatory prison term. Related unchanged 1034 permits AG civil actions with a PREPONDERANCE conduct proof and penalty capped at the GREATER of $50,000 per violation and the received/offered compensation amount, with specified remittance and nonexclusive-remedy terms; its injunctive route requires the stated court finding after the AG reason-to-believe petition. The bill does not invent new penalty amounts, dispense with those elements, establish first-ever illegality of insurance/bond fraud or conclusively decide whether an existing bond practice was already insurance. It does not alter a detainee release/bond entitlement, bond minimum, detention/removal grounds, immigration status or the legal authority to adjudicate an immigration case. The printed Federal immigration bail-bond phrase is not newly defined or exhaustively equated to one INA bond category here. Application of the retained insurer/commerce/authorized-consent construction to a particular cash, charitable or federal-bond arrangement remains an explicit legal-review dependency. The whole one-insertion bill covers monetary/criminal bail as well as immigration bonds; the choice is not a separate vote on an immigration component or a finding about any actual bond organization. One H.R. 6260 episode. No actual conviction, detention, release, fraud, prevention of violence or enactment is established by the House result.
